To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) dendritic cell (CD11c(+) 33D1(+) F4/80(+) CD11b(+)) cells can be isolated from mouse brain by culturing primary brain cells in the presence of granulocyte macro- phage-colony stimulating factor (GM-CS) and that (b) the function of such brain-derived dendrific cells depends on astroglial support.

dendriform cells are induced by GM-CSF in mouse brain primary culture; they are CD11c+ and express the myeloid marker F4/80, but not the lymphoid marker CD8alpha; they are functionally active as APC when freshly isolated, but their function is lost during sub-culture; their functional activity is maintained when cultured in the presence of astrocyte-conditioning medium; this activity co-fractionated with M-CSF, and neutralization of M-CS
dendritic cells (DC) are present in the brain and their antigen presentation function depends on astrocytic help.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a novel class of antigen presenting cells (APC), which we have named dendriform cells (DC) and which are characterized by the presence of a dendritic morphology, the expression of a variety of surface markers and the ability to present exogenous antigens.
the role of GM-CSF in the development and maturation of dendritic cells.
the antigen presentation function of brain dendriform cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
astrocytes, in the presence of M-CSF, help the differentiation of dendriform myeloid cells in the brain.
astrocytes play a role in the maintenance and function of brain-derived APC, which is mediated through M-CSF.
GM-CSF-growth of brain-derived dendritic cells depends on astroglia help.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GM-CSF induces the development of immature DC in brain, but that astrocytes are necessary for maintaining their antigen presentation capability.
the brain is endowed with an APC population that is dependent on astrocyte-derived M-CSF to preserve their antigen presentation function.
the brain-derived APC, which are not yet fully functional, require the help of astrocytes to acquire their antigen presentation function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in addition, to GM-CSF astrocyte-derived M-CSF is essential for the development of functionaly active APC.
the antigen presentation capability of brain-derived APC is maintained by astrocyte-secreted M-CSF.
brain-derived dendrific cells, which are induced in primary culture by GM-CSF, are immature DCs and their functional activity requires astrocyte-derived M-CSF.
